core_obligations: Reduce to bounded above test complexes (proof lines 3126-3140): for an acyclic L^bullet use L^bullet = colim_m tau_{<= m}L^bullet termwise, so Tot(K^bullet tensor L^bullet) is the termwise colimit of the Tot(K^bullet tensor tau_{<= m}L^bullet), and it suffices to prove each of those acyclic; each tau_{<= m}L^bullet is still acyclic.
Apply the spectral sequence (proof lines 3141-3146): in the bounded above case the first quadrant spectral sequence of the double complex has E_1^{p,q} = H^p(L^bullet tensor K^q).
Finish (proof lines 3146-3148): each E_1^{p,q} vanishes because K^q is flat and L^bullet is acyclic, so the total complex is acyclic and K^bullet is K-flat.
proof_roadmap: Test K-flatness against an acyclic complex L^bullet.
Write L^bullet as the termwise colimit of its truncations, so only the bounded above case has to be handled.
In the bounded case the first quadrant spectral sequence converges and its E_1 terms are H^p(L^bullet tensor K^q).
Flatness of K^q and acyclicity of L^bullet kill every E_1 term, so the total complex is acyclic.
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that a bounded above complex of flat modules on a ringed site is K-flat (statement lines 3119-3123). The proof needs one reduction and one spectral-sequence computation: an arbitrary acyclic test complex is written as the termwise colimit of its truncations so that only bounded above test complexes have to be considered (proof lines 3126-3140), and in the bounded case the first quadrant spectral sequence of the double complex has E_1^{p,q} = H^p(L^bullet tensor K^q), which vanishes because K^q is flat and L^bullet is acyclic (proof lines 3141-3147). The non-formal content is the colimit reduction, which is also where boundedness of K^bullet is used. The claim is H2: one reduction plus one standard spectral-sequence identification.
